qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: French retail banking structure prevents independent pricing power: fixed-rate mortgages lag rate cycles while regulated savings accounts (Livret A) mandate funding floors. Standalone loan and mortgage underwriting operates as a commodity, resulting in sub-hurdle multi-cycle ROE (8-9%) failing the 12% requirement.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (REJECT). Crédit Agricole possesses immense domestic scale and strong bancassurance fee engines (Amundi, Predica), but French retail banking lacks structural pricing power due to long-term fixed-rate mortgage contracts, statutory usury rate caps (taux d'usure), and state-mandated savings rates (Livret A). 10-year average ROE of ~8.5% fails the 12% GAAP hurdle across the cycle.
qualitative.evidence: Crédit Agricole S.A. (CASA) anchors France's leading retail banking network and Europe's largest asset manager (Amundi). While recent ROTE has reached ~13.5-14% supported by bancassurance fees and CIB, its 10-year average ROE sits at 8.2%-9.2% (dropping to 4.5% in 2020 and 6-7% in 2016-2017). The French retail network experienced severe margin compression when ECB rates rose due to fixed-rate loan portfolios and mandated pass-through deposit costs.
